$BNB swung hard, covering about a 9.5% range in 24 h while it usually hugs a 3.2% band, that's more than double its normal swing.

$UNI was even messier, jumping roughly 19.4% all day versus a typical 7.5% move, so it's also more than twice the usual spread.

$SOL didn't lag far behind, bouncing close to an 11.9% range compared with its average 4.8%, again, over twice the everyday volatility.

All three busted out of their normal windows; nothing else stood out today.

$SHELL's gone wild, up 52.34% to $0.02995, trading between $0.01965 and $0.05163 with almost $39 M in volume. Meanwhile $SOXLB crumbled, down 12.936% to $55.86, its range squeezed from $66.91 to $52.43 on $43 M volume. $ZEC also slipped, losing 9.058% to $885.07, bouncing between $992.98 and $876.64 with $155 M changing hands. Leaders sprinting, laggards tumbling, just the 24-hour story.

$NVDAB slipped to 161.42 USDT, down 1.507% after hitting a high of 171.59 USDT. Volume sat around 149.6 M USDT, so the move kept rolling through the night.

Sandisk's token, $SNDKB, took a deeper tumble, 861.04 USDT now, a 6.981% drop from its peak at 946.58 USDT. Trade activity was lighter, about 28.7 M USDT, but the dip held steady past regular market close.

Tesla's bStock, $TSLAB, hovered near 387.65 USDT, down 2.574% after a brief pop to 404.54 USDT. With roughly 3.34 M USDT changing hands, the price kept drifting in after hours.

All three kept moving while traditional exchanges were offline, just another 24/7 crypto-style grind.

$SPCXBUSDT slipped about 1.7% and its 24-hour swing was roughly 4.36%, noticeably tighter than its usual ~6% daily range, about a third less volatile than normal.

$PEPEUSDT dropped 2.9% and only moved around 7.73% in the last day, which is also somewhat tighter compared with its typical ~9.8% swing.

$XRPUSDT slid 2.5% and saw a 4.59% range, basically in line with its average 4.83% range, so nothing out of the ordinary there.

All three were down, but the first two kept their moves a bit more contained than they usually do.

$NEAR surged 2.4% to $3.51, hitting a high of $3.64 while volume topped $90 M. Meanwhile $BTC slipped 3.9% to $68 893, pulling back from a $71 750 peak and still churning $2 B in trade. $HYPE managed a modest 2.2% rise to $72.78, touching $75.35 on the upside. Leaders are climbing, BTC's the biggest drags. Looks like the alt-run's outpacing the king today.

$BARD surged almost 90% to $0.1625, trading near its high of $0.1799 after a wild swing from $0.0853. Meanwhile $BTC slipped 3.6% to $69,300, pulling back from a $72,288 peak and hovering close to its low of $67,568. $ETH also fell, down 1.4% at $1,964, stuck between a $2,028 top and $1,896 floor. Big volume on the leader, tiny pullbacks on the majors, just a classic 24-hour swing.

$BTC's at $68,731, down 6.9% in 24h, slipped from a high of $73,866.72 and barely nudged above $68,527.89. $ETH sits around $1,930, also down 6.1%, fell from $2,056.73 and found support near $1,917.01. $BNB traded at $632.42, lost 6.8%, peaked at $679.03 and lingered just above $630.13. Volume's still decent, $BTC around 22,265 BTC, $ETH over 317k ETH, $BNB about 164k BNB, so liquidity's there. Watch if any of these levels hold; a break back toward the day-highs could test the upside, while staying near the lows would keep the pressure on. Nothing wild, just a solid pull-back across the board.

$NVDABUSDT surged 2.89% to 166.98, punching up to a high of 168.56 while volume hit 266.9 M. $GOOGLBUSDT wasn't far behind, climbing 2.889% to 299.55 and topping out at 302.79 on 22.9 M quote volume. Meanwhile $NEARUSDT slipped 6.601% to 3.396, barely breaking its low of 3.341 and trading 69.9 M in volume. The leaders are charging ahead, the laggard is pulling back hard. Just a quick snapshot of who's riding the wave and who's getting left in the wake.

$NVDAB is sitting at 164.97 USDT, down 5.97% after hitting a high of 176 and a low of 149.23. Volume's hefty at 276.3 M USDT, so the pullback's well-filled even though the market's asleep.

S&P 500 ETF's token $SPYB barely budged, 759.69 USDT with a 0.12% dip. The range stayed tight, high 763.55, low 753.8, and 1.85 M USDT traded, proof the bStock keeps moving 24/7 while the floor's closed.

Sandisk's $SNDKB dropped 5.88% to 935.12 USDT, swinging from a 998.7 high down to 870.83. Still, 32.8 M USDT swapped hands, showing the token's liquidity survives the off-hours grind.

All three bStocks are doing their thing around the clock, no big surprises, just the usual after-hours flow.

$BTC slipped to $71,652.98, down 2.56% in 24 h, after hitting a high of $74,811.45 and testing the low at $71,293.23. $ETH is at $2,006.51, off 2.28%, with a swing between $2,103.78 and $1,983.82. $BNB fell hardest, sitting at $653.34, down 4.00% after a brief pop to $689.30 and barely breaking $650.01. Volume's still decent, $BTC traded about 15,871 BTC, $ETH moved roughly 250 k, $BNB around 122 k. Keep an eye on whether $BNB can hold above $650; $BTC and $ETH look set to linger near today's lows. Just a flat-lined morning across the board.

$SNDKBUSDT jumped 4.7% to $947.7, carving out a tight range between $897.6 and $1,011.1 with almost $79.2 M in quote volume. $GRAMUSDT nudged up 3.1% to $1.18, holding a band from $1.127 to $1.257 and pulling in $27.2 M. Meanwhile $PEPEUSDT slumped 14.9% to $0.00000457, skidding between $0.0000045 and $0.00000537 while still racking up $79.5 M of volume. One side's pushing higher, the other's getting hammered.

$BTC slipped to $73,586, down 0.19% after peaking at $74,811. The dip stayed within a tight $73,209-$74,811 range, volume around 16.2k.

$ETH slid to $2,042, a 0.45% drop, after testing $2,104 earlier. It bounced off $2,035-$2,104 lows-highs, with roughly 191k trades moving $395M.

$BNB barely budged, holding $678.07, up 0.07% from yesterday. It hovered between $676.77 and $689.30, 78k volume pushing $53.8M.

All three sat near their 24-hour lows, no big breaks. Keep an eye on whether any token cracks the upper edge of its range.

$BTC nudged up 1.33% to $74,356, hitting a high of $74,780 before easing back to a low of $73,209. Volume steadied around 14.3 K, moving roughly $1.06 B in quote terms.

$ETH outpaced it a touch, climbing 1.70% to $2,077.69, topped out at $2,103.78 and found support near $2,038.53. Trading was busy, 189 K coins swapped, pushing $390 M of USDT.

$BNB posted the strongest percent gain, up 1.76% to $685.98, with a tight range between $673.26 and $689.30. 76 K BNB moved, translating to $52 M in quote volume.

Watch the $BTC order book depth as price tests the $74,780 ceiling again; any break could reshape the short-term spread.

$ETH/$BTC is at 0.02787, down 0.606% versus BTC. Meanwhile $BTC slipped 0.119% in USD terms, so the whole market's a bit softer. The 20-coin basket, however, nudged up 0.447% overall, meaning the average alt outperformed BTC today. ETH is losing a touch of relative strength to BTC, while the broader alt set is holding a slight edge. Nothing wild, just a modest tilt toward the alt basket and a small bleed for the big guys.

$INIT surged 62% to $0.288, hitting $0.332 at the high and dumping a hefty $35.6 M in quote volume. $ONE jumped 25% to $0.001745, with a peak of $0.00208 and $28.1 M flowing through. Meanwhile $ZEC slipped 10% down to $1 030, still swinging between $1 200 and $994 and moving a massive $256 M. Gains are blasting off while $ZEC's taking the hit. Looks like the short-term winners are tiny-cap rockets, and the big-cap miner is feeling the pressure.

$SNDKBUSDT slipped about 3.8% and only swung 10.2% today, versus its usual 11.8% range, that's roughly a third tighter than normal.

$NEARUSDT dropped just under 1% and moved 8.1% in the last 24 h, a shade tighter than its typical 8% swing, so it's a bit more constrained.

$BTC stayed around $73,931, down 1.5% with a 3.67% daily range, pretty much in line with its average 3.63% range, nothing out of the ordinary.

Overall, the market's been a little more restrained on those pairs, but no big moves to flag.

$BTC slipped to $73,418, down 1.665% after hitting a high of $75,442.01. Volume was about 16.3k BTC, moving $1.21 B in quote terms.

$ETH fell harder, landing at $2,043.54, a 3.764% drop from the day's peak $2,143.44. It traded 328,908 ETH, pushing $681 M in quote volume.

$BNB edged lower too, closing at $674.40, off 1.887% from its $692.64 high. Activity clocked 127,461 BNB, about $87.4 M in quote volume.

Watch the $BTC order-book depth as it approaches the $73k-$74k zone; any shift there could set the tone for the next session.

$INIT exploded, up about 138% to $0.31109, trading between $0.12658 and $0.315 with ~25.7 M USDT swapped. Meanwhile $SOL slipped 3.4% to $84.15, its range narrowed to $82.61-$88.07 on a hefty 177.9 M volume. $AVAX also fell, down 5% to $8.39, low of $8.23, high $9.01 and 43.9 M USDT moved. One pair rockets, the others lose steam. Looks like a mixed bag today.

$SOXLBUSDT surged 22.2% to $54.86, bouncing from a low of $41.32 up to $57.76 on heavy volume. $AVAXUSDT followed with a 7.5% jump, trading at $8.57 after hovering between $7.81 and $9.01. Meanwhile $ZECUSDT slipped 6.1% to $1,156.57, sliding from a high of $1,235.99 down to $1,142.34 despite the biggest quote volume in the set. The market's pulling ahead on the bullish side while the losers are getting squeezed. Looks like a split-personality day.

$BTC slipped a hair to $75,078, down 0.02% after testing $75,599. The 24-hour range was $73,750-$75,599 on ~15.3k BTC volume. $ETH fell 0.75% to $2,126, hitting a high of $2,160 and a low of $2,083 with ~291k ETH traded. $BNB nudged up 0.37% to $689, staying between $673 and $693 on about 116k BNB volume.

Watch the $BTC price action around the $75,600 resistance; a break could set the tone for the next session.

$BTC slid to $74,920, down 0.6% after hitting $75,734.51 and testing $73,510. Volume sat around 19.5 k, so liquidity stayed decent.

$ETH dropped 3.9% to $2,128.36, a pull from the $2,214.83 high; the low was $2,060. With 431 k coins traded, the market showed real appetite despite the dip.

$BNB nudged lower, ending at $690.09, off 0.5% from the $693.73 peak, and bounced off $673.31. About 165 k BNB changed hands, keeping the quote volume near $112 M.

All three slipped a bit, no wild swings, just a modest pullback across the board.

$SOXLBUSDT exploded 20.6% to $55.15, trading near its $55.43 high after a swing from $41.32. $AVAXUSDT added 8.5% to $8.96, still hugging the $9.00 ceiling. Meanwhile $ETHUSDT slipped 4.3% to $2,144, down from a $2,243 peak and hovering close to its $2,060 trough. Leaders are roaring, laggards are bruised, just a typical 24-hour swing.

$NVDAB slipped 3.8% to 180.15 USDT, hugging its low of 177.61 after hitting 188.06 earlier. Volume's sitting around 10.6 M USDT, so the token's still seeing decent action 24/7.

Tesla's bStock, $TSLAB, nudged up 0.95% to 361.66 USDT, trading just shy of its day-high 362.9 and staying above the 352.98 low. 867 K USDT moved through the pair in the last session.

Micron's $MUB is up 0.77% at 697.86 USDT, edging toward its 707.75 peak while staying above the 664.35 floor. 14.6 M USDT of volume shows the token's got plenty of liquidity around the clock.

All three bStocks are bouncing in crypto-time, no market close to wait for.

$BTC up 0.108% while the 20-token basket slipped about 1.34%, so Bitcoin's pulling ahead of the alt pack. $ETH's price in BTC fell 0.136%, meaning it's losing ground to Bitcoin directly. ETH's still hovering around 0.02941 BTC. Overall, BTC's the only one posting a gain; the rest of the top alts are in the red. Nothing wild, just Bitcoin edging out the crowd and ETH slipping a bit against it.

$BTC slipped to $75,710, down 0.097% in 24 h, hugging its low of $75,571 after a brief pop to $76,200. Volume held near 5,100 BTC, so the move wasn't a flash-sell.

$ETH lingered around $2,226, down 0.343% with a high of $2,246 and a low of $2,223.1. Trading about 56,800 ETH, the market stayed tight; nothing broke the range.

$BNB edged up to $695.95, +0.206% after testing $702 before settling near $693.9. Volume topped 52,700 BNB, showing a modest buy-side bite.

All three sat in narrow bands; watch if any breaks past today's highs or lows for the next cue.

$ETH slipped 0.169% against $BTC, so it's losing a bit of relative strength. $BTC rose 0.196% in USD, but the 20-coin basket nudged up 0.308%, edging out the king. Alt average outpaced $BTC, while $ETH fell behind its own benchmark. Nothing wild, just a small shuffle of relative gains.

$ONE swung hard, covering about 40 % of the price range in the last 24 h, that's more than twice its normal daily swing of ~18 %. $ZEC barely budged, its 24-hour range sat at roughly 8 % versus a typical 10 % span, so it stayed close to usual. Nothing crazy beyond the ONE burst; just a quick, noisy ride.

$ONE surged 46.8% and ripped through a 38.6% range in the last 24 h, that's more than twice its usual daily swing, so the token moved a lot more than typical.

$ZEC slipped about 5.8% while its price window stayed around 9 % today, essentially the same as its weekly average, so nothing out of the ordinary there.

$XRP edged down 1.5% in a tight 2.9% band, well under its normal 4.5% range, meaning it was pretty calm.

Just a quick heads-up on the wild swing for $ONE and the steady vibe for the others.

$ONE surged 43.7% to $0.002267, hitting a high of $0.002476 after slipping down to $0.001546 earlier. $UNI nudged up 1.7% to $7.056, trading between $6.861 and $7.105. Meanwhile $ZEC fell 7.2% to $1,265.01, its low was $1,250.90 and it barely broke $1,368 on the upside. Leaders are ripping through the low-volume zone, laggards are dragging in the heavy-volume crowd. Nothing wild, just a clear split between the rockets and the sinkers.

$ONE is buzzing, its 24-hour swing hit about 38.9%, almost three times its usual 14% range. That's a lot of movement for a token that's usually steadier.

$SNDK barely nudged out of its norm, trading in an 11.36% band versus an 11.06% average, basically the same as any other day.

$XRP's range actually squeezed a bit, 4.11% compared with a typical 4.48%, so it stayed tighter than usual.

Just a quick snapshot, $ONE's the only one that really broke out of its comfort zone.
